subject: Data retention exception request - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: data handling / retention follow-ups

Hi Jane — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

What we heard: Acme needs a hard guarantee that PII related to user requests (names, emails, phone numbers) is not retained in logs or KV cache and that any analytical logs are either zero-retention or limited to a very short window. You also flagged the need for evidence (controls and test results) and a contract-level commitment for the retention schedule.

Redwood recap / options: 
- Hosted API: we can configure shortened operational logs (24–72 hrs) and PII redaction at the ingestion layer; full 0-retention for PII is not available on hosted without reducing observability.
- Dedicated or Private deployment: we can support a 0-retention configuration for request payloads and turn off persistent KV caching. This typically requires a Private deployment or a Dedicated reserved pool with an addendum.

Attachments: I attached a retention matrix and a draft SOW that outlines Private deployment + retention addendum as one pathway.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether Acme would accept a Private deployment (VPC) + retention addendum, or if you require this for Hosted?
2) If Private is acceptable, we'll scope an engineering change (deletion hook + redaction filter) and put together a redline for the SOW and SLA. Estimated time: 2 sprints for implementation + compliance signoff.
3) Please share any legal language you'd prefer in the retention addendum.

Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up with our engineering lead to walk through the technical controls. 

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: data handling / retention follow-ups

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary. We appreciate the options. A few clarifications/questions from the security team: 

1) Our requirement: 0-retention for any PII present in request/response payloads. That includes both request text and any derived completions that contain PII. We also want to ensure KV cache is never persisted for these requests. 
2) If Hosted cannot provide 0-retention, can Redwood guarantee that the KV cache will not contain PII and that logs are purged within X hours? We'd prefer X = 0 but would consider <= 24 hours for non-PII analytics only. 
3) Data residency: All logs and storage must remain in the US. Does Redwood support region-locking in Dedicated? 
4) Evidence: can you provide configuration docs, a proposed redline for the SOW/contract, and any existing compliance artifacts (SOC 2 audit report or summary) for our security review?

We are under a tight procurement timeline — would like to have contractual language and technical evidence by next Thursday. If Private + addendum is the only path to 0-retention, please flag the expected timeline and cost delta.

Thanks,
Jane Doe
Security Lead | Acme Corp
jane.doe@acme.com

Looping in Rafael to scope the engineering ask. Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few notes from security/compliance perspective: 

- Private (VPC/on-prem) is clearly the cleanest mechanism to guarantee 0-retention for PII because the customer controls storage and we can disable all persistent logging hooks. 
- For Dedicated (Redwood-managed hardware), we can implement a retention addendum that enforces immediate redaction/deletion of PII fields and disables KV persistence for covered routes, but we need to enumerate which routes are in-scope and accept reduced observability (less token-level tracing).
- We will need legal to sign an addendum that includes the retention schedule and an acceptance test (evidence of deletion + audit logs).

Rafael — can you confirm technical feasibility and provide an ETA for a retention addendum implementation (deletion hooks + configuration options)? Also include whether we can offer a temporary Hosted compromise (e.g., redact on ingest + 24-hour analytic logs) while we provision Dedicated/Private.

Thanks,
Camila
Head of Security & Compliance (sales-support) | Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: data handling / retention follow-ups

Short answer: feasible with caveats. Implementation notes: 

- Private deployment: we can implement a configurable ingestion filter that strips or hashes PII fields prior to any persistence. We can also disable KV cache persistence entirely for the customer namespace. This meets Acme's 0-retention ask. Engineering effort: approx 2 sprints (3 weeks) to harden and add the necessary deployment automation and test harness. Compliance evidence: we can produce an acceptance test run and a config snapshot for their audit.

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): we can support near-0 retention by applying the same filter on ingest and deleting operational logs on a 24–72 hour schedule. However, some ephemeral internal traces used for debugging may persist until the job-level deletion window runs — we can scope to reduce this but cannot guarantee complete zero bytes without Private.

- Hosted API: recommend a temporary compromise where we redact PII at ingestion and keep analytics logs at 24 hours for a short pilot. This allows them to start quickly while we stand up Dedicated/Private.

Impact on observability: turning off persistent logs and KV cache will reduce our ability to trace individual request latency and token-level breakdowns. We should capture that tradeoff in the SOW and a runbook for incident response.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Draft a retention addendum describing the deletion hook, scope of routes, acceptance test, and rolling timetable. (I'll draft a technical appendix.)
2) Provide Acme with a pilot config for Hosted redaction + 24hr analytics if they want to begin sooner.
3) If Acme agrees to Private, get legal contact and we'll produce a cost delta and timeline.

I attached a retention addendum draft and the retention matrix. Rafael
Engineering Lead, Solutions | Redwood Inference
